final_proof:
**Proof.**

Two mappings with the same domain $S$ and codomain $\R$ are equal if and only if they agree at every point of $S$. So fix an arbitrary $s \in S$, and write $a = \map f s$, $b = \map g s$, both real numbers.

By the definitions of the pointwise operations,
$$\map {\paren{\tfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}}} s = \tfrac 1 2 \paren{\map f s + \map g s + \size{\map f s - \map g s}} = \tfrac 1 2 \paren{a + b + \size{a - b}}.$$
Indeed, $\map {\paren{f-g}} s = a - b$, so $\map {\size{f-g}} s = \size{a-b}$. Then $\map {\paren{f+g+\size{f-g}}} s = a + b + \size{a-b}$, and scalar multiplication by $\tfrac12$ multiplies this value by $\tfrac12$.

Also $\map {\paren{f \vee g}} s = \max\set{a, b}$. So it is enough to prove the real-number identity
$$\max\set{a,b} = \tfrac 1 2 \paren{a + b + \size{a - b}} \quad\text{for all } a, b \in \R.$$

Since $\R$ is totally ordered, either $a \ge b$ or $a < b$.

*Case $a \ge b$.* Then $a - b \ge 0$, so $\size{a-b} = a - b$, and
$\tfrac12\paren{a + b + (a - b)} = \tfrac12 \cdot 2a = a = \max\set{a,b}$.

*Case $a < b$.* Then $a - b < 0$, so $\size{a-b} = -(a-b) = b - a$, and
$\tfrac12\paren{a + b + (b - a)} = \tfrac12 \cdot 2b = b = \max\set{a,b}$.

The identity holds in both cases. Hence $\map {\paren{f \vee g}} s = \map {\paren{\tfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}}} s$ for every $s \in S$, and therefore
$$f \vee g = \dfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}. \qquad \blacksquare$$
